lines.japanese:
翡翠の声で目が覚めた。
　あれから―――屋敷に帰ってきたあと、自分の部屋に引き込んで眠ったのだろう。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
Hisui’s voice wakes me.
Afterward—after returning to the mansion—I must have shut myself in my room and fallen asleep.
lines.mao_english:
Hisui’s voice wakes me.
Afterward—after returning to the mansion—I must have shut myself in my room and fallen asleep.
lines.mirrorMoon:
I wake up to the sound of Hisui's voice.
Since then----after returning to the mansion, I must have made my way to my room somehow and slept.
lines.mirror_moon:
I wake up to the sound of Hisui's voice.
Since then----after returning to the mansion, I must have made my way to my room somehow and slept.

lines.japanese:
「志貴さま、なにかご気分がすぐれないのですか？」
「――――いや。
別に、何も」
　返答して、ベッドから起きあがる。
　……自分でも、呆れるぐらい。
　何も口にしたくないのに、体はいつも通りに生活をしようとする。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki, are you feeling unwell?”
“—No. I’m fine.”
I answer and get out of bed.
Even I can hardly believe it.
I don’t want to say a word, yet my body insists on going through life as usual.
lines.mao_english:

I don’t want to say a word, yet my body insists on going through life as usual.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Shiki-sama, are you not feeling well?"
"----No, I'm fine."
Answering, I sit up in bed.
…… I'm almost amazed at myself.
I don't even feel like talking, but my body tries to start my day as always.

lines.japanese:
「朝食だろ。
すぐに行くよ」
「………はい。
それではお待ちしております」
　何か言いたそうな顔をして翡翠は退室する。
　着替えて、居間にむかった。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
“Breakfast, right? I’ll be there in a minute.”
“Very well. We shall be waiting.”
Hisui leaves with something unspoken on her face.
I dress and make my way to the sitting room.

"……… Yes.
I will be waiting."

居間には秋葉と琥珀がいた。
「おはよう」
　いつも通りの挨拶をして、食堂に向かう。
　朝食を口にして、居間に戻る。
　そのままソファーに座って、ぼんやりと時計を眺めた。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
Akiha and Kohaku are in the sitting room.
“Good morning.”
I offer the usual greeting and go into the dining room.
I eat breakfast and return to the sitting room.
I sit on the sofa and stare vacantly at the clock.

「……兄さん？
　その、今日は学校があるってわかってますよね？」
「うん―――？
　ああ、そっか。
学校には、行かないといけないよな」
　忘れていた。
　なにもやる事がなくなったから、あとはこのまま、ずっとヌケガラのまま生きていくんだって、ぼんやりと思っていたけど。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
“…Brother? You do realize there is school today, don’t you?”
“Mm—? Oh. Right. I have to go to school.”
I had forgotten.
With nothing left for me to do, I had vaguely imagined that I would go on living like an empty shell forever.

　何も言わず、登校することにした。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
“I still have Shiki Tohno’s life to live, after all. If I have nothing else to do, I may as well go to school.”
“Brother?”
Akiha gives me a suspicious look.
I can’t even be bothered to make up an excuse.
Without another word, I leave for school.

…… Speaking is just a pain.
Without saying anything, I go to school.

lines.japanese:
何の異状もなく時間は流れていく。
　こうして何時間めかの授業を、何の目的もなく受けている。
　かつかつ、というチョークの音。
　黒板にせわしなく書かれていく数式を、無意識にノートに書き写していく。
　ふと、窓の外から裏庭を見た。
　当然のように、そこには誰もいない。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
The hours pass without incident.
I sit through yet another class with no purpose at all.
Chalk taps against the board.
My hand copies the equations appearing there in a hurried stream, though my mind takes in none of them.
On impulse, I look through the window at the rear courtyard.
Naturally, no one is there.

I emptily attend my lessons.
The sound of the chalk.
I mindlessly write down what's written on the board into my notes.
I look out the window into the rear courtyard.
Of course there's no one there.

「――――――」
　―――何をしているんだろう、俺は。
　こんなところで、おとなしく授業なんか受けたりして。
　あいつを探しもしないで、普通の学生に戻ってしまって。
lines.label: s194
lines.maoEnglish:
“————”
―――What am I doing?
Sitting obediently in a classroom.
Not even searching for her, simply returning to life as an ordinary student.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirror_moon:

　だから、本当に。

So it’s true.
I have lost Arcueid.

ばき。

“…………”
The sound came from my desk.
It’s nothing.
I merely gripped my mechanical pencil too hard and snapped it again.

「遠野、ちょっと来なさい」
　教壇から数学の教師が声をかけてくる。
「―――はい、なんですか」
　返事をして教壇に向かった。
lines.label: s194

Class ends.
The room fills with noise, but I remain at my desk exactly as I was during the lesson.
“Tohno, come here a moment.”
The mathematics teacher calls from the lectern.
“—Yes? What is it?”
I answer and walk to the front.

“…I do. I had business in town after midnight these past few days.”
“—I see.”
The mathematics teacher—who is also our homeroom teacher—frowns, then looks almost apologetic.

Go to the discipline office after school. Consider it bad luck and bear with them.”
With that, the teacher leaves the classroom.
